title: Cap. 1 prol. IV: distinguishing conditions defined — free-will use
pass_a_gloss: Now concerning distinguishing conditions a few things also are to be said. IV. I call distinguishing conditions contrary acts or qualities which, when foresight and preconsidered in the subject, contrary acts also are exercised in God concerning the same subject. For example, the good use of free choice and the bad use of free choice are contrary acts: If therefore anyone should hold that from the foresight of the good use, according to God's ordination, humans are always predestined, and from the foresight of the bad use are reprobated, that person makes the good and bad use of free choice into distinguishing conditions required in the subject of predestination or reprobation. Key lemmas: conditiones distinguentes (distinguishing conditions); praevisio (foresight); liberum arbitrium (free choice); praedestinari / reprobari.
pass_b_english: A few words now on distinguishing conditions. IV. By distinguishing conditions I mean contrary acts or qualities which, when foresight and weighed beforehand in the subject, bring about contrary acts in God toward that same subject. Take free choice: its good use and its bad use are contrary acts. If someone holds that, by God's ordination, foresight of the good use always means predestination, and foresight of the bad use means reprobation, then that person makes the good and bad use of free choice into distinguishing conditions required in the subject of predestination or reprobation.
source_text: Jam de conditionibus distinguentibus pauca etiam dicenda sunt. IV. Conditiones distinguentes appello, contrarios actus aut qualitates, quibus in subjecto praevisis & praeconsideratis, contrarii actus etiam in Deo circa idem subjectum exercentur. Verbi causa, bonus usus liberi arbitrii, & malus usus liberi arbitrii sunt actus contrarii: Si quis ergo sentiat ex praevisione boni usus secundum Dei ordinationem homines semper praedestinari, ex praevisione mali usus reprobari, is facit bonum & malum usum liberi arbitrii conditiones distinguentes in subjecto praedestinationis aut reprobationis requisitas.
